dirtySanta.title: Dirty Santa Rules
dirtySanta.subtitle: The classic gift exchange with a secret and a funny present.
dirtySanta.intro: Dirty Santa is the simplest version of the gift exchange: everybody buys a present for somebody else, and nobody knows who has to buy for whom.

rules.0: Everybody writes one present on a slip of paper and puts it into a hat.
rules.1: Everybody draws one slip and buys exactly the present that is written on it.
rules.2: Nobody may buy a present for the person who drew them, and nobody may draw their own name.
rules.3: The value of the presents should be the same for everybody.
rules.4: The presents are opened one after the other, so the funny gifts are the highlight of the evening.
rules.5: Only the person who bought the present knows the rules, so the surprise stays until the end.

whiteElephant.title: White Elephant Rules
whiteElephant.subtitle: The gift game in which every present may change its owner.
whiteElephant.intro: White Elephant is played with wrapped presents that everybody may open, swap and give away again.

rules.0: Everybody brings one wrapped present and puts it into the circle in the middle of the table.
rules.1: Everybody draws a present and may open it right away.
rules.2: A present that has already been opened may be taken away and swapped for another one.
rules.3: The present that was taken away has to be opened by the next person who draws it.
rules.4: The game ends when everybody has had a turn and the last present is opened.
rules.5: The best present of the evening may be kept, the rest goes back into the circle.

yankeeSwap.title: Yankee Swap Rules
yankeeSwap.subtitle: The Christmas game in which the presents change their owner twice.
yankeeSwap.intro: Yankee Swap is played in two rounds: first the presents are handed out, then they are swapped once.

rules.0: Everybody writes the name of a person of the family on a slip and puts it into a hat.
rules.1: Everybody brings a present and writes the name of the person who receives it on it.
rules.2: Everybody draws a name blind and gives the present to the person who owns it.
rules.3: The person who bought the present secretly takes the present of somebody else and gives it away.
rules.4: The value of the presents should be the same for everybody.
rules.5: After the swap everybody opens the present that is now in front of them.

ConstructionTools.rectangleCircleTriangleAreaFormulas: Rectangle = length × width · Circle = π × radius² · Triangle = (base × height) ÷ 2. Square metres = sq ft × 0.092903 · Acres = sq ft ÷ 43,560.
ConstructionTools.cubicFeetAndCubicYardsWithBagYields: cubic feet = length × width × (depth ÷ 12) · cubic yards = cubic feet ÷ 27 · an 80 lb bag yields about 0.60 ft³, a 60 lb bag 0.45 ft³.
ConstructionTools.tonsAndGravelDensities: Tons = (area × depth in feet ÷ 27) × density. Pea gravel is about 1.4 tons per cubic yard, crushed stone about 1.35 and sand about 1.3.
ConstructionTools.mulchCubicFeetAndCubicYards: cubic feet = area × (depth ÷ 12) · cubic yards = cubic feet ÷ 27.
ConstructionTools.tileAreaIncludesTheGroutJoint: Tile area includes the grout joint: (length + grout) × (width + grout) ÷ 144. Tiles = area ÷ tile area, plus the waste allowance.
ConstructionTools.wallAreaAndGallons: Wall area = perimeter × height − doors − windows. Gallons = area ÷ coverage × coats. One gallon covers roughly 350 sq ft.
ConstructionTools.pitchMultiplierAndRoofingSquares: Pitch multiplier = √(1 + (pitch ÷ 12)²). One roofing square is 100 sq ft; three squares make a bundle of shingles.
ConstructionTools.bTUBaseWithCeilingsOccupantsAndKitchen: Base = 30 BTU per sq ft · high ceilings add 5 BTU per sq ft · each occupant adds 300 BTU · a kitchen adds 1,200 BTU. One ton of cooling equals 12,000 BTU.

Epley and Brzycki are the most accurate for sets of 10 reps or fewer. The chart lists the 1RM implied by lifting the same weight for each rep count, and that weight as a percentage of your estimated 1RM.
